title: Anti-CEC protests: Who qualifies as a journalist? SC to examine issues involving protection for scribes

ai.summary: The Supreme Court will examine who qualifies as a journalist and whether self-proclaimed reporters should have greater protection than accredited journalists during protests, following allegations of police misconduct against media covering anti-CEC demonstrations in Delhi.

facts.claim: The Supreme Court will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited mediapersons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests
facts.quote: The Supreme Court on Thursday said it will consider who qualifies to be a journalist and whether accredited mediapersons should enjoy greater protection than self-proclaimed reporters while covering protests.

facts.claim: The Supreme Court asked a committee to examine petitions over the alleged detention of seven journalists, assault, and obstruction of journalists covering protests in Delhi on 10 and 11 October 2026
facts.quote: The top court asked the high-powered committee headed by former top court judge R Subhash Reddy to examine petitions over the alleged detention of seven journalists, assault, and obstruction of journalists covering protests in Delhi on 10 and 11 October 2026.

facts.claim: The Delhi Police stated that reel-makers cannot automatically claim the protections given to the press while covering protests
facts.quote: Social media content creators cannot automatically claim the protections given to the press while covering protests, the Delhi Police submitted.

facts.claim: The Delhi Police submitted that it had to be determined if reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters
facts.quote: It had to be determined if "reel-makers can be elevated to the status of journalists or reporters", the police said.

ai.background_note: The Supreme Court is addressing concerns about journalist protection during anti-CEC protests in Delhi, following allegations of police misconduct against media covering demonstrations.
